_comment: Cascade spectacle (#187), read by screen code only. A heat tier is on once the cascade has lit minNodes dominoes or a cap of at least minCap (its value per trigger, from the capFired event) has gone off; the last tier on sets the colour and how many sparks trail each flow. While building, the same tiers read the board's node count and the biggest charge on an open end. Tier colours are 0xRRGGBB strings.

dominoLook.comment: Domino drawing (#217), read by src/game/dominoDrawing.ts. Positions are in mockup units (an amplifier bar is 100 high, the whole amplifier 216 wide, the socket on the left edge, the centre line at y 50); the screen size is units times unit. extent is each kind's width and height in units, for layout. Details (owner stripe, rarity gem, upgrade star) are hidden when the domino is shown below minDetailScale of full size; number, sockets and outputs always stay.

buildup.comment: Cascade build-up (#191). pitch.maxSteps: the pitch stops rising after this many cascade steps. glow: strength of the lit dominoes' glow, from litMin (first lit) to litMax (all lit). strip: height of the strip at the top of the board mat kept free for the counter and callouts (the tree is laid out below it); counter.at and callouts.at are where in the mat's width they are centred, so each screen's own mat sets where they go. They stay put on screen whatever the camera does. callouts.list: the running damage that fires each word, once each, at most max per cascade (the highest newly crossed fires; lower ones are used up with it). camera: boards with more than minNodes dominoes ease out (to zoomOut, or what fits the board mat, never below minZoom) and push in on a new biggest cap of at least push.minCap (push.reducedZoom with reduced flashing; no push with screen shake off); the camera never cuts off health, block or the intent card (keep: sizes of the boxes it protects and of an open end). Callouts: holdFraction of ms they stay, then fade; fadeInMs, popMs, startScale, popScale shape the burst. Times are ms at 1x.

seatColours.comment: One colour per seat, by seat order. Chosen to differ from each other, from the six spark colours and from the gold turn highlight.

comfort.comment: Defaults for the menu comfort settings.

fx.comment: Code-drawn fallbacks for the effect textures (fx/<id>). glow and ring are always code-drawn.

projectiles.comment: Effects that fly from a cap to their target (#189). A shot is one trigger of a cap. At most maxOnScreen shots of each kind are in the air at once; further triggers fold into the newest shot of that kind (its x-count and size grow). A shot uses the last tier whose minValue it reaches: size in pixels, travelMs at 1x (bigger is faster), gain (impact loudness 0..1). Colours are 0xRRGGBB strings; sizes are pixels unless a factor of the tier size.

speedControl.comment: Combat playback speed button and its list (#220), read by src/game/speedControl.ts. Px on the 1920x1080 table. Where the button sits comes from combatLayout.footer (#231); the list opens upward, gap above it, and opens downward instead if it would leave the screen.

setOffPreview.comment: Set-off preview on the health bars (#222), read by src/game/setOffPreview.ts. Px on the 1920x1080 table. The ghost is the part of a bar the set-off would take; it pulses between alphaLow and alphaHigh every pulseMs (steady at alphaHigh under reduced flashing). The bars and shields it draws on come from the column (combatLayout, through the scene's refs) and the Set off button from combatLayout.actions.setOff. Label offsets are from the bar's right edge, the shield or the safe mark. Skull and crack numbers are fractions of the skull radius or the shield size.

enemyReactions.comment: Enemy reactions (#190), read by src/game/enemyReactions.ts. Times are ms at 1x (scaled by playback speed), distances px on the 1920x1080 table. A hit of at least staggerMin damage staggers instead of flinching. The ghost bar waits delayMs after the last hit, then drains to the real value at perPointMs per point (between minMs and maxMs), so a run of hits shares one drain. Shield cracks show at each crack fraction of the block worn down.

fuseBoard.comment: Fuse board (#229), read by src/game/fuseBoard.ts. Lengths are px at the board scale (scale, a share of full size) and the whole tree shrinks together (never below minScale) only when it outgrows its area. The owner stripe stays down to detailScale. gap: run between a domino's edge and the next one; rowPitch: distance between branches; ringRadius: the open-end ghost ring; padLeft: space left of the opener inside the area so its socket ring is not clipped; openerCharge: the charge an opener starts with (the engine's start charge, which no view exposes), only to colour a live number red or green on the opener slot; junctionGapX: where a junction's middle output (Hall of Mirrors) leaves, in domino units. fuse: dark under-stroke and spark-colour stroke widths, bend (share of the run used as the curve's handle), the cascade's burnt part (burnWidth, burnAlpha, burnMs at 1x). badge: the charge pill at a fuse's midpoint; nudge lists the places along the fuse (0..1) tried in order until it clears every tile, ring and other badge by clearance. ring: dashed open end, its gold charge badge, the legal highlight (pulse is skipped with reduced flashing); lock: the padlock on a locked end. live: the result bubble beside an end while a hand domino is hovered or dragged (good = at or above its base, bad = below it); dimAlpha for ends it is not aimed at. opener: the empty first slot.

handFan.comment: The fanned hand (#229), read by src/game/handFan.ts. scale: a hand domino's resting size (shrunk, never below minScale, when a big hand would overlap more than minStepFactor of a domino's width); stepFactor: how far apart (a share of a domino's width) they sit before they are squeezed into the area; degPerDomino / maxSpread: fan angle; arc: how far the ends sit below the middle. The hovered domino straightens, grows to hoverScale and lifts by lift (tweenMs). gap: the faint dashed place left by a dragged domino (the domino itself fades to holderAlpha). enter: a new draw slides in from the deck (slideMs for an old domino finding its new place, enterMs from the deck, staggerMs between new ones). area: the rectangle the fan sits in (between the piles and clear of Pass and Set off at x1610; the middle domino's centre is the middle of it). piles: the deck on the left and the discard on the right, each a rectangle (the pile is drawn at its middle and the rectangle is its click area), drawn at pile scale with their count and label.

combatLayout.comment: Combat screen layout (#228, #231 Spotlight; the board rectangle is the fuse board's area and the cascade counter's strip is its top, #229; the hand's place is handFan.area and handFan.piles), read by CombatScene.ts, columnLayout.ts, enemyUnit.ts, setOffTally.ts, turnRail.ts and combatHud.ts. Px on the 1920x1080 table; boxes are x, y top-left with w, h. Colours are #rrggbb. The column is stacked top to bottom from its content: the portrait card shrinks first (between card.minH and card.maxH) when the stack runs short, then the gaps between sections shrink (never below column.minGap; they grow to column.maxGap when there is room). Bars, shields, the enemy's body and the set-off preview all follow from the column: nothing else repeats their places. The seat tabs run across the top right of the column; the board is below them, the hand and actions at the bottom.
